question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` accept scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and what exact wildcard grammar is acceptable for Gateway browser-origin authorization?
rationale: The requested behavior changes which browser origins can reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket handling, and the current documented contract intentionally limits wildcard behavior to the global `*`.

options.title: Approve constrained wildcard grammar
options.body: Define a narrow list of allowed scheme-pattern forms, implement it once in `checkBrowserOrigin`, and document positive and negative cases before accepting the feature.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the existing global `*` escape hatch for intentionally broad local testing.

options.title: Defer to broader pattern design
options.body: Wait for loopback-origin pattern work to settle, then decide whether Chrome extension scheme wildcards belong in the same contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained wildcard grammar
recommendation.body: Define a narrow list of allowed scheme-pattern forms, implement it once in `checkBrowserOrigin`, and document positive and negative cases before accepting the feature.
